item.title: Int'l seminar explores CPC's self-governance practices, global implications
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
Int'l seminar explores CPC's self-governance practices, global implications Qu Qingshan, president of the Institute of Party History and Literature of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, addresses an international seminar on understanding the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Cai Yang) BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- An international seminar on understanding the recently concluded key Communist Party of China (CPC) plenum was held in Beijing on Friday, bringing together more than 200 diplomats, think tank experts and media representatives from 105 countries and international organizations. At the seminar, a report titled "Putting the People First -- Values Underpinning Full and Rigorous Self-Governance of the CPC" was jointly released by the national high-level think tanks of the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee and Xinhua News Agency. EXPOUNDING ON THE PLENUM The seminar focused on the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, with participants discussing the CPC's achievements and the significance of full and rigorous Party self-governance, governance through institutions and rules, and principle of putting the people first. In his address, Qu Qingshan, president of the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee, said the plenary session was a highly important meeting held at a crucial stage in China's efforts to basically achieve socialist modernization. The session made strategic plans for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, fully demonstrating the CPC Central Committee's strong sense of historical initiative in strengthening the Party and the country, Qu said. Fu Hua, president of Xinhua News Agency, said that guided by the Resolution of the Central Committee of the CPC on Certain Major Issues concerning Persevering with Full and Rigorous Party Self-Governance, adopted at the plenum, the CPC will continue to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance from a new historical starting point, further strengthening its capacity to govern and its leadership capabilities. Fu also said that Xinhua stands ready to work with all parties to deepen systematic and theoretical research and interpretation of major issues concerning Party building in the new era and help the international community better understand China and the CPC. Lyu Yansong, Xinhua's editor-in-chief, said that as China strives to build a great modern socialist country and achieve its second centenary goal, sustained efforts to strengthen Party self-governance are essential to ensuring that the CPC remains a strong leadership core in the cause of socialism with Chinese characteristics. The resolution adopts a systematic approach, with its various measures designed to reinforce one another in terms of objectives, implementation and outcomes, ensuring that the Party's governance practices keep pace with the times, follow established principles and embrace innovation, said Huang Yibing, vice president of the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee. SHARING INSIGHTS ON GLOBAL SIGNIFICANCE International participants shared their perspectives on the CPC's governance practices and their implications for political parties around the world. Zafar Uddin Mahmood, special representative of the prime minister of Pakistan on China affairs, said China's governance model and its ability to maintain institutional continuity, implement long-term plans and respond to new challenges have attracted widespread international attention. Patricio Giusto, executive director of the Observatory of Argentina-China Relations, said the CPC had offered an effective and resolute response to corruption from within -- one of the oldest challenges associated with political power. The CPC has built its political practice on strict discipline, stable institutional norms and sound intra-Party regulations, he said, adding that keeping power within the bounds of institutions is one of the key pillars of its success in Party governance. Josef Gregory Mahoney, a professor of politics and international relations at East China Normal University, said the CPC had long recognized that unchecked corruption and pointless formalities could erode public trust and undermine its governing capacity. The CPC regards improving intra-Party regulations as a long-term and fundamental approach to advancing full and rigorous self-governance, a practice worthy of study by political parties in other countries, he said. The seminar was co-hosted by the Institute of Party History and Literature of the CPC Central Committee and Xinhua News Agency. item.title: China passes law against cross-border corruption, ratifies agreement on establishing World AI Cooperation Organization
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
China passes law against cross-border corruption, ratifies agreement on establishing World AI Cooperation Organization Zhao Leji, chairman of the National People's Congress (NPC) Standing Committee, presides over the closing meeting of the 25th session of the 14th NPC Standing Committee at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhang Ling) BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- Chinese lawmakers on Friday voted to adopt a law against cross-border corruption, a law on procuratorial public-interest litigation, and ratify an agreement on establishing the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization. The votes were taken at a closing meeting of the 25th session of the Standing Committee of the 14th National People's Congress (NPC) in Beijing. Lawmakers also voted to adopt a law on Antarctic activities and environmental protection, a revised Water Law, and a decision on amending 15 laws, including the Emergency Response Law. They also adopted a decision to remove Li Lecheng from the post of minister of industry and information technology. President Xi Jinping signed five presidential orders to promulgate the laws and the decision, and a sixth one to announce the decision on the personnel change. Zhao Leji, chairman of the NPC Standing Committee, presided over the closing meeting. The meeting also voted to adopt reports on the examination of deputies' proposals and on the qualification of certain deputies and other personnel-related bills. Addressing the closing meeting, Zhao stressed the need to uphold higher standards and adopt more concrete measures to improve the efficacy of Party building within the people's congress system, while urging further improvements to the legal framework for combating corruption. He also chaired a meeting of the Council of Chairpersons of the NPC Standing Committee before the closing meeting, and presided over a lecture for lawmakers afterward. item.title: Xi says a growing China can be partner to help Europe tackle challenges
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
Xi says a growing China can be partner to help Europe tackle challenges Chinese President Xi Jinping meets with Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker, who is on an official visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu) BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- A growing and developing China is not the source of Europe's problems, but a partner that can help Europe address its challenges, said Chinese President Xi Jinping during his meeting with Austrian Chancellor Christian Stocker in Beijing on Friday. Xi stressed that China and Europe should focus on areas of cooperation, resolve economic and trade frictions through dialogue and consultation, and achieve win-win results and common development. Noting that this year marks the 55th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and Austria, Xi said trust and friendship are the valuable features of China-Austria relations, transcending differences in social systems, history, culture and development stages. He called on the two sides to consolidate political mutual trust, sustain the positive momentum of high-level exchanges, enhance mutual trust and dispel misgivings through communication, and lay a solid political foundation for future cooperation. Xi said that during the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) period, China will foster emerging industries, upgrade traditional industries, and further expand opening-up, with a focus on the service sector. China Opportunity 2.0 will bring not only market dividends but also innovation dividends, he noted. China stands ready to work with Austria to expand practical cooperation in emerging fields such as new-energy vehicles, artificial intelligence, digital economy and green development, and foster new engines for economic and trade growth, Xi said. Noting that China-Austria friendship enjoys extensive public support, Xi said the two sides should expand people-to-people and cultural exchanges, facilitate personnel flows, and bring the peoples of the two countries even closer. Stocker said that Austria is committed to fostering its friendly strategic partnership with China, and adheres to the one-China policy. Stocker called on the two countries to build on the long-standing cooperation and mutual trust to comprehensively strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, science and technology, innovation and other fields, boost cultural, tourism and other people-to-people exchanges, and elevate bilateral relations to new heights. He said Austria actively supports the development of EU-China relations and hopes both sides can resolve economic and trade differences through candid dialogue and consultation. Austria is ready to work with China to uphold multilateralism, strengthen multilateral coordination, advance sustainable development, tackle challenges including climate change, and safeguard global prosperity and stability, added Stocker. item.title: China, Gabon elevate ties to community with shared future for new era
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
China, Gabon elevate ties to community with shared future for new era Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema, who is on a state visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping held talks with Gabonese President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema in Beijing on Friday. The two leaders announced the elevation of bilateral relations to a China-Gabon community with a shared future for the new era. Noting China is willing to be a reliable friend and partner for Gabon in its independent development, Xi said China supports Gabon in maintaining independence in political, economic and diplomatic affairs, and will join hands with Gabon to build a China-Gabon community with a shared future for the new era. Xi said China is ready to work with Gabon to maintain close communication at all levels, exchange experience in political party and state governance, and support Gabon in strengthening its governance capacity. Hailing the strong economic complementarity and great potential for cooperation between the two countries, Xi called on both sides to strengthen the alignment of their development strategies and cultivate new growth drivers for cooperation. He called for making good use of the new opportunities presented by zero-tariff treatment of African goods and the "green channel" facilitation measures for African agricultural and food products exported to China. Both sides should expand and upgrade bilateral trade and investment cooperation to support Gabon's industrial development, job creation, and livelihood improvement, thereby enhancing the country's capacity for independent economic development, Xi said. "The vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity and the four major global initiatives I have proposed serve, first and foremost, the common interests of the Global South and African countries," Xi said, adding that China supports Gabon in playing a greater role in international and regional affairs. Nguema said Gabon firmly adheres to the one-China principle, and hopes to draw on China's successful experience in governance of party and country. He said Gabon stands ready to further deepen practical cooperation with China, and welcomes more Chinese enterprises to invest and do business in Gabon to help Gabon achieve industrialization and sustainable development. Noting that China has established a mutually beneficial and win-win partnership with Africa, Nguema said the zero-tariff policy meets the needs of African countries, enabling African products to enter the vast Chinese market, which is of historic significance to the development of African countries. He added Gabon is willing to work with China to enhance solidarity and cooperation between Africa and China and jointly safeguard the interests of Global South countries. After the talks, the two heads of state witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents covering the implementation of the Global Security Initiative, zero-tariff treatment, industrial and supply chains, Chinese language education, and other fields. During Nguema's state visit to China, the two sides issued a joint statement on building a China-Gabon community with a shared future for the new era. Prior to the talks, Xi held a welcome ceremony for Nguema in the Great Hall of the People. Xi also held a welcome banquet for him in the evening. item.title: Xi votes in local legislative election in Beijing
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-07
Xi votes in local legislative election in Beijing Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, casts his ballot to elect deputies to the Xicheng district people's congress at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Xicheng District of Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi) BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping cast his ballot at a polling station in Beijing on Friday to elect deputies to a local people's congress. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, voted at the Huairentang polling station of the Zhongnanhai electoral district in Xicheng District to elect deputies to the Xicheng district people's congress. Xi stressed efforts to practice whole-process people's democracy, uphold Party leadership, and strengthen oversight throughout the election process to ensure that deputies who meet the people's expectations are elected. Around 3:30 p.m. Friday, Xi arrived at the polling station, gave his voter registration card to staff for verification, and got a ballot. He cast his ballot after filling it. Noting that the election of deputies to people's congresses is an important foundation for upholding, improving and practicing the people's congress system, Xi underlined the need to give full play to democracy, strictly act in accordance with the law, and ensure that the election is carried out fairly and cleanly. On Friday afternoon, other senior Chinese leaders Li Qiang, Zhao Leji, Wang Huning, Cai Qi, Ding Xuexiang and Li Xi cast their ballots in person, while Han Zheng entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Former Chinese leader Hu Jintao also entrusted a staff member to vote on his behalf. Friday saw people vote at 13,054 polling stations across Beijing to elect 4,898 new deputies to the people's congresses at the district level and 11,137 deputies to the township-level people's congresses. Chinese Premier Li Qiang, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, casts his ballot to elect deputies to a local people's congress at the Ziguangge polling station of the Wenjin Street electoral district in Xicheng District of Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 6, 2026. item.title: Global media leaders call for closer dialogue, coordination amid security challenges
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
Global media leaders call for closer dialogue, coordination amid security challenges BEIJING, Nov. 5 (Xinhua) -- Chinese and foreign media representatives attending the 7th World Media Summit in Beijing on Thursday called for stronger dialogue and cooperation to address global security challenges and promote common development. A forum on powering intelligent media was held on the sidelines of the summit, bringing together participants to discuss how media can leverage advanced technologies, build consensus and contribute to global security and shared development. Ren Weidong, deputy editor-in-chief of Xinhua News Agency, said in his address that media outlets should not be bystanders or onlookers in the face of global security challenges, but should strive to shoulder their responsibilities. Media should serve as guardians of factual reporting, adopters of advanced technologies, disseminators of diverse voices and promoters of exchanges and cooperation, helping pool collective wisdom to safeguard global security and promote sustainable development, Ren said. Abdul Hakim, president director of Indonesia's Antara News Agency, said opportunities created by advances in energy infrastructure and computing capacity should benefit developing countries, and digital transformation should enable more people outside major cities to gain access to credible information. People should embrace innovation while upholding principles, and news production should be accurate, fair and honest, he said. Participants of the forum also called for stronger cooperation in sharing technological achievements and building professional capabilities, promoting the development of artificial intelligence in a safer, fairer and more inclusive direction. The 7th World Media Summit, co-hosted by Xinhua News Agency and the People's Government of Beijing Municipality, is to be held from Nov. 5 to 9 in Beijing. Under the theme "Media in the Intelligent Age: From Consensus to Action", the summit brings together nearly 500 delegates from nearly 330 mainstream media outlets, think tanks, government departments and international organizations from 112 countries and regions around the world. The mechanism of the World Media Summit was initiated in 2009 and is an important global platform for high-end media exchange and cooperation. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: China to extend anti-dumping, anti-subsidy tariffs on US NPA imports for five years
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
China to extend anti-dumping, anti-subsidy tariffs on US NPA imports for five years BEIJING, Nov. 5 (Xinhua) -- China will extend anti-dumping and anti-subsidy duties on imports of n-Propanol (NPA) from the United States for a further five years starting Friday, the commerce ministry said Thursday. NPA is an industrial chemical used mainly as a solvent and as an intermediate in chemical manufacturing. Under the extended measures, anti-dumping duties range from 254.4 percent to 267.4 percent, while the anti-subsidy duties range from 34.2 percent to 37.7 percent, according to two ministry notices. The decision follows two expiry reviews covering separate anti-dumping and anti-subsidy measures. The ministry found that dumping and subsidisation involving U.S. NPA imports could continue or recur if the duties were lifted, potentially causing damage to China's domestic industry to persist or recur. China first imposed the duties in November 2020 for a five-year period. It launched expiry reviews in November 2025 at the request of domestic producers. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: Report highlights China's role in global marine biological diversity governance
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
Report highlights China's role in global marine biological diversity governance This photo taken on Oct. 15, 2026 shows coral pictured through the porthole of the manned deep-sea submersible Jiaolong. (Xinhua/Li Xin) BEIJING, Nov. 5 (Xinhua) -- China has shared its expertise and taken practical steps in support of the conservation and sustainable use of marine biological diversity, said a report released Thursday. The country, by helping bridge differences between developed and developing countries, has advanced the conclusion of a landmark agreement in global ocean governance, namely the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction, which entered into force early this year, according to the report released by the China Institute for Marine Affairs under the Ministry of Natural Resources. In designing and refining relevant legal arrangements, China has advocated a benefit-sharing mechanism encompassing both monetary and non-monetary benefits to safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of developing countries, and supported an integrated approach to biodiversity conservation and the sustainable use of marine resources, said the report. China has promoted greater procedural transparency, and advocated a country-driven and needs-based approach and diversified cooperation forms to strengthen developing countries' implementation capacity. As one of the first signatories and Parties to the Agreement, China has taken practical steps to support its full and effective implementation. The report noted that China has made its research platforms accessible to international partners and shared scientific results with them through scientific research expeditions conducted using its deep-sea submersibles such as Jiaolong and Fendouzhe, as well as research vessels like Shenhai Yihao. China has preserved nearly 60,000 samples of marine microbial resources and established repositories and databases, and offered specialized services to facilitate access to samples and data, the report said. China has supported developing countries in environmental impact assessment. It has also signed marine cooperation agreements with more than 50 countries and international organizations, jointly established over 40 marine research centers and laboratories, and implemented numerous small-scale, high-impact marine conservation projects, strengthening the ocean-related capabilities of the Global South, the report revealed. By applying to host the Secretariat of the Agreement in the coastal city of Xiamen in east China's Fujian Province, the country has undertaken further international responsibilities in an effort to address the absence of headquarters of United Nations ocean-related bodies in Asia, according to the report. item.title: Super buyer China opens door to shared prosperity at import expo
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
Super buyer China opens door to shared prosperity at import expo This photo taken on Oct. 26, 2026 shows a view of the south square of the National Exhibition and Convention Center (Shanghai), the main venue for the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), in east China's Shanghai. (Xinhua/Fang Zhe) SHANGHAI, Nov. 5 (Xinhua) -- Amid rising protectionism and waning faith in free trade, China is staging two major international trade expos back-to-back, signaling its steadfast commitment to continuous opening up. The ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), the world's largest import-themed expo, opened in Shanghai in east China on Thursday, just a day after the export-focused Canton Fair concluded in south China's Guangzhou, shifting the spotlight to China's increasingly prominent role as a global super buyer. Running from Nov. 5 to 10, this year's CIIE has attracted 4,142 overseas exhibitors. With Canada and Sri Lanka as guest countries of honor, the ninth edition of the expo features more than 300 Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders. Across the bustling expo floor in Shanghai, sprawling over a total area of 440,000 square meters, exhibits range from cutting-edge technologies, such as a 6G terminal prototype and a high-precision turn-mill machine, to everyday consumer goods, including food, cosmetics and clothing, ready to test their potential in China's supersized market. This photo taken on Nov. 4, 2026 shows the exhibition area of Intelligent Industry and Information Technology of the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) in east China's Shanghai. (Xinhua/Guo Lei) MAGNETIC CIIE In 2018, as China's per capita GDP approached the 10,000-USD mark, the country launched the CIIE, a trade fair dedicated to imports, as a gateway for businesses to tap into the world's second-largest consumer market. Over the years, many innovative drugs exhibited at the CIIE have seen their market entry into China accelerated. Exotic food exhibits, meanwhile, have since enjoyed the media spotlight and found their way onto Chinese dining tables. According to Shanghai Customs, since the inaugural CIIE, more than 100 varieties of fruit from over 40 countries have gained access to the Chinese market. Once exotic fruits, from Malaysian durians to Peruvian blueberries, are now a common sight on Chinese supermarket shelves. For many exhibitors, the tangible benefits of past participation keep them coming back year after year. This year, nearly 200 businesses and institutions are returning for their ninth consecutive CIIE. One such "full-attendance" exhibitor, U.S. materials science giant Dow, values CIIE as a platform to "showcase its capabilities, understand market needs and expand value-chain partnerships," Puay Koon Chia, Dow Asia Pacific president, told Xinhua. Opportunities created by the platform have also reached many small businesses that have traditionally struggled to enter unfamiliar foreign markets. A staff member organizes alpaca wool products at a booth of the Consumer Goods exhibition area of the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) in east China's Shanghai, Nov. 4, 2026. (Xinhua/Du Xiaoyi) Ali Faiz, a carpet dealer from Afghanistan, first attended the CIIE in 2020 with just 20 or so carpets. Since then, orders from China have helped improve the livelihoods of more than 1,500 carpet-weaving families in his home country. To help exhibitors navigate market opportunities, this year's CIIE has built on existing initiatives, such as buyer-seller matchmaking events, the Hongqiao International Economic Forum, and a range of dialogues and cultural activities. It has also introduced new features, including a dedicated exhibition section for time-honored national brands from around the world. SUPER BUYER CHINA The CIIE's magnetic pull stems from China's growing role as a global super buyer, underpinned by its 1.4-billion population, its people's rising purchasing power and their growing appetite for a better quality of life. China has remained the world's second-largest import market for 17 consecutive years, with its total imports exceeding 90 trillion yuan (about 13.4 trillion U.S. dollars) during the 14th Five-Year Plan period (2021-2025). The pace is picking up. China's imports reached 16.7 trillion yuan in the first nine months of 2026, up 22.3 percent, the fastest growth since 2021. This photo taken on Nov. 4, 2026 shows the Dedicated Showcase for National Brands Worldwide at the Food and Agricultural Products exhibition area of the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE), in east China's Shanghai. (Xinhua/Wang Xiang) Beyond a supersized market, more sophisticated consumer demand in China is creating fresh opportunities for global businesses. From healthier diets and beauty products to outdoor sports and leisure experiences, China's growing middle-income population is embracing new lifestyles and driving demand for a wider range of goods and services. A newcomer to the CIIE, outdoor apparel brand Arc'teryx has gained momentum in China in recent years. John Yin, senior vice president-general manager of Arc'teryx Greater China, cited the country's thriving outdoor sports culture as among the underlying drives for the company's "longstanding commitment to China's market." A classic example of an emerging lifestyle in China reshaping global trade is the import of coffee beans. Long known for its tea-drinking traditions, China has emerged as one of the world's fastest-growing coffee markets. As coffee culture spreads from major cities to smaller towns, surging demand is driving imports of coffee beans from growing regions around the globe. For African coffee exporters, from Ethiopia to Mauritius, the CIIE offers a gateway to this swiftly expanding market. Adding to their optimism is China's zero-tariff treatment of imports from all 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic relations, which took effect on May 1. This year's CIIE features an upgraded Asia-Africa products zone designed to help African countries capitalize on the zero-tariff policy, while expanding free exhibition space for the least developed countries by 17 percent. Beyond the expo, China's commitment to opening its market wider is also reflected in its policy blueprint. Promoting balanced growth in imports and exports has been written into the outline of the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030). Meanwhile, this year's government work report calls for boosting imports to promote balanced trade. This goal also aligns with a shift in domestic economic priorities that sees consumption taking on a greater role as a stabilizing anchor and key driver of growth. China this year laid out its first five-year plan dedicated to expanding consumption, setting a goal of raising total retail sales of consumer goods to around 60 trillion yuan by 2030. According to Sourabh Gupta, a senior fellow at the Institute for China-America Studies, the CIIE sends two important messages: China's commitment to a more balanced, higher-quality growth model driven primarily by domestic demand, and its willingness to become as impressive an importer as it is an exporter, thereby contributing to global economic rebalancing. "TEST GROUND AND A GYM" Exhibitors at the CIIE, including those with a long-standing presence in the country, increasingly see China as more than just a consumer market. It is also a testing ground for innovation and a launchpad for products that aspire to reach consumers worldwide. This photo taken on Nov. 4, 2026 shows a booth of the Automobile and Smart Mobility exhibition area of the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) in east China's Shanghai. (Xinhua/Han Xiaoyu) "China is both a test ground and a gym, a place where we test new ideas, challenge ourselves and continuously strengthen our innovation capabilities," Jay Wu, Michelin China vice president, director of government relations and strategy, told Xinhua. He noted that new trends and technologies in sectors ranging from electric vehicles to autonomous driving often emerge in China ahead of other markets. Unveiling a tire made with 75 percent renewable and recycled materials at the CIIE, the French tire manufacturer described its evolving approach to China as a shift from "In China, for China" to "With China, for the World." This shift reflects a broader trend among multinational companies. At a press conference in October, a Chinese National Bureau of Statistics official said more foreign firms are embracing "China Opportunity 2.0" by integrating more deeply into the country's industrial and innovation chains. The trend extends beyond industrial manufacturing to consumer goods, where increasingly sophisticated Chinese consumers are helping shape global innovation. Stéphane de La Faverie, president and CEO of the Estée Lauder Companies, noted in his videotaped message to the CIIE that as China continues to set the pace for beauty innovation, the country is not only an important market, but also "a source of talent, insight and inspiration." Maziar Mike Doustdar, president and CEO of Novo Nordisk, echoed his view. "China is becoming an increasingly important source of innovation. We are excited to bring China-originated innovation into our growing pipeline and explore its potential to benefit patients worldwide." For the Danish pharmaceutical giant, which has participated in every edition of the CIIE, China's rapidly evolving pharmaceutical innovation landscape and expanding healthcare market have reinforced its confidence in investing in the country. As Doustdar put it: "Investing in China is investing in the future." Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.
